title: Compute Systems: VMs, GKE, Serverless, VMware Engine, and Orchestration
bodyMarkdown:
## Provisioning Compute and Orchestrating Infrastructure

The architect chooses the compute model, the pricing model, the networking, and the automation that keeps fleets patched and reproducible.

### The compute spectrum

| Option | Manages for you | Use when |
|--------|-----------------|----------|
| Compute Engine | Nothing above the VM | Full OS control, legacy/lift-and-shift, GPUs/TPUs |
| Google Cloud VMware Engine | Managed VMware SDDC (vSphere/vSAN/NSX) | Lift-and-shift VMware estates unchanged |
| GKE Standard | Control plane; you manage node pools | Fine-grained cluster control, special hardware/daemonsets |
| GKE Autopilot | Control plane + nodes; pay per Pod request | Hands-off Kubernetes |
| Cloud Run | Everything; scale to zero | Stateless containers, request-driven, jobs |
| Cloud Functions | Everything | Event-driven small functions |

**Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE)** runs a fully managed VMware Cloud Foundation stack on dedicated nodes — true lift-and-shift keeping vCenter/vSAN/NSX, with a later modernization path. Contrast with **Migrate to Virtual Machines**, which converts VMware VMs into native Compute Engine instances (re-platforming).

### Pricing and provisioning models

- **On-demand** — no commitment; **sustained-use discounts** apply automatically on Compute Engine.
- **Committed Use Discounts (CUDs)** — 1- or 3-year resource/spend commitments for steady, always-on baselines (large savings, no interruption).
- **Spot VMs** — deepest discount (~60-91%) but preemptible with no SLA; ideal for fault-tolerant, checkpointed batch in a **managed instance group**.
- **Sole-tenant nodes** — physical isolation for licensing/compliance.
- **Reservations / Dynamic Workload Scheduler** — guarantee accelerator/VM capacity.

**Decision:** steady 24/7 -> CUDs; interruptible batch -> Spot; predictable peaks above baseline -> on-demand.

### Cloud-native networking for compute

- Compute Engine uses VPC subnets, internal/external LBs, and Cloud NAT.
- **GKE** uses VPC-native (alias IP) clusters with secondary ranges for Pods/Services, **NEGs** for container-native load balancing, and Gateway/Ingress.
- **Serverless** (Cloud Run/Functions) reaches VPC resources via **Serverless VPC Access connectors** or **Direct VPC egress**.

### Container orchestration

GKE provides Horizontal/Vertical Pod Autoscaling, Cluster Autoscaler, node auto-provisioning, and multi-cluster fleets. Use **Autopilot** to remove node operations entirely; use **Standard** when you need privileged workloads or specific node shapes.

### Infrastructure orchestration and patch management

- **Infrastructure Manager** — Google's **managed Terraform** runner with state and IAM integration.
- **Cloud Foundation Toolkit (CFT)** — opinionated, reusable Terraform blueprints aligned to best practices.
- **Config Connector** — manage Google Cloud resources declaratively as Kubernetes objects.
- **VM Manager** — fleet **OS patch management**, OS inventory, compliance reporting, and OS policy/script execution across projects via the OS Config agent.

### Best practices

- Treat infrastructure as code; store Terraform state remotely with locking.
- Use MIGs for self-healing and autoscaling; bake golden images and patch with VM Manager.
- Match each tier to the cheapest model that meets its availability needs.
